scope: Bounded USB ZLP reads and intermediate XFlash status frames; host tests plus limited read-only r1 observations.

bulk_transport.fixture_change: Two immediate-zero-read rejection cases are replaced by bounded read-ZLP cases; zero-write and exception rejection remain.

read_correction.scope: Actual extracted read/command-handler/CLI chain; query/storage/initial command modeled except dedicated command control.

limits: A successful zero-length exact USB read consumes the original endpoint-call and monotonic-time budgets; exceptions are never retried.

Intermediate raw-zero statuses are restricted to eMMC storage 1 and 512-aligned address, selected length and current byte offset. One status per offset bounds the total by length/512; four-byte payload data is unsupported.
Header datatypes, global status parsing, other DA protocols, partition selection and physical media durability remain outside this change.
A drained zero-status frame or a newly opened USB handle alone does not prove protocol quiescence.
The finite engineering budgets cannot preempt an uncooperative USB backend and may reject slow valid operations.
Old packages and prepared scripts retain their old transport pins until explicitly refreshed.
